messages:
Shivani: Heads-up — rough proposal for mixed-capacity pools to reduce cost while limiting tail-impact of spot interruptions. Idea: per-region min on-demand floor that staggers across AZs + small hot burst pool in each AZ with fast pre-warm handoff. Thoughts?

Anne: High level makes sense. Can we quantify 'min floor' as percent of baseline GPU count or as running QPS SLO? Which should be primary?

Joel: Finance angle — prefer % of committed baseline, because it maps to reserved commit and billing. Ballpark: min-floor = 15% per region cuts cost ~20% vs all-on-demand in sims but interruptions go up. Need trade curves.

Oliver: Technical note — hot burst pool can't throw away KV affinity. If we move an ongoing generation mid-run, we lose KV cache and latency/cost spikes. We need sticky routing or a shared cache tier for handoff.

Tyler: SRE: regional network drain sometimes adds 30–60s to node shutdown in eu-west1; that kills short-lived gens. We need faster SIGTERM path: drain traffic, checkpoint, shutdown <10s for preemptible lanes. Also consider fallback to smaller model instead of killing request.

Shivani: Agree on sticky routing. Two-pronged: 1) per-AZ sticky lanes for generation lifetime (pin session to node), 2) quick-drain hook in agent to flush minimal KV or mark session for graceful tail-handoff.

Anne: Can agents reliably write partial KV? Consistency risk. Alternative: classify long sessions as non-preemptible and keep them on-demand; short ones go to burst.

Oliver: We can estimate token length cheaply. Heuristic + light ML classifier at router; if est_tokens > 512, pin to on-demand. Should be low CPU.

Joel: Cost sketch: long sessions are ~12% of requests but ~40% of tokens. Pinning those to on-demand (20% capacity) increases baseline cost ~+6% but drops interruption-exposed token volume ~65%. Might be acceptable.

Tyler: Operational guardrail: interruption credits per-tenant to prevent noisy neighbors from burning the burst pool. Suggest token-based credit bucket with refill tied to committed spend or reserve tier.

Shivani: Draft router rules prototype below — simple YAML for discussion:

```
rules:
  - name: long_session_pin
    condition: estimated_tokens >= 512
    action: route_to: on_demand
  - name: burst_default
    condition: estimated_tokens < 512
    action: route_to: burst_pool
  - name: regional_floor
    condition: region_capacity_pct < floor_pct
    action: reserve: on_demand_pool
```

Anne: Good. Metrics we should track: interruption_rate (by region/az), avg_shutdown_duration, token_cost_per_request, pct_requests_pinned, KV_hit_rate_on_handoff.

Tyler: Add runbooks: 'spot-drain-shortgen' (handle short gens during drains) and 'burst-oversubscribe' (mitigate when burst pool exhausted). Also add synthetic that simulates network-drain delays.

Shivani: Rollout plan suggestion: prototype in staging eu-west1 with 2-week alpha. We'll run A/B: baseline vs staggered-floor + burst. Need telemetry and cost sims.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Next available window: 2025-04-02 03:00 UTC to run staging deploy. :calendar:

Oliver: I'll own router classification + sticky routing. Adding telemetry for estimated_tokens label and pin decisions.

Joel: I'll run cost sims for floor_pct = [10,15,20,25] and share curves by EOD Friday. Will include impact on reserved commit utilization.

Anne: SGTM. Tyler, can you open the two runbook PRs?

Tyler: On it. PRs created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/482 & https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/483 :thumbsup:

Shivani: :thumbsup: Thanks all. Reconvene after Joel's sims and Oliver's telemetry added.
